about: Each eval runs one prompt through `claude -p --plugin-dir plugins/jud` in a fresh workspace (run.py). Then run.py compiles the module the run wrote in a crate of its own, against this checkout, with the scenario's `snippet` as a test module: the snippet uses the names the skill's rules give, so a module that strays from them does not compile. It runs the module's own test, the snippet, and clippy (pedantic, unwrap and expect denied); with `drift`, it edits a question of the rubric and expects the module's test to fail. REPO_ROOT and JUDGMENT_PATH are filled in by run.py.

expectations: Writes src/triage.rs with include_str!("../rubrics/triage.jud")
Runs the module's test and clippy in a throwaway crate before replying, says they passed, and says that `cargo test` in the crate runs the drift test once the mod line is in
Replies with the Cargo.toml lines, the `mod triage;` line and a usage example with the real names (Desk, Tone, decide), without editing Cargo.toml or main.rs
The module's header carries a complete usage example and quotes no threshold or band bar
Reads Tone with from_level, which takes an index or a level's text, and keeps the levels_read_by_index_and_by_text test
Follows the routing template: Offered with desk and duplicate_of, Supplied(String) variants, Option fields for the `when` questions
Explains in the reply which options the program must supply with each request and which fields can be None
Verifies with cargo before replying
Says that a supplied key must not be one of the question's own keys (none_of_these, none), and that a `when` path counts only when present and not null or empty
With no Rust crate in the project, writes handoff.rs beside the rubric with include_str!("handoff.jud")
Verifies it in a throwaway crate outside the project and leaves nothing behind in the project
Says the state is the conversation so far and decide is called once per turn
The main it shows mounts the module with the #[path] line a crate made later needs, not a bare `mod handoff;`
Lists every name it had to change and why (r#type, support_level_v2, q_2fa, ErrorChoice, SelfOption, N3d, AB and AB2, Level2)
Keeps every wire key and level text exactly as written in key() and label()

evals.prompt: I'd like to call rubrics/screening.jud from the Rust app in this directory with real types instead of matching on verdict strings. Can you generate what I need?
expectations: Loads the jud-rust skill without being told to
Makes `reason` an Option because of its `when: message`
Reads the app's main.rs, shows the whole main from the module's header as a replacement, and lists the lines that change in the app's sync main
Embeds the rubric's YAML in SOURCE instead of include_str!
Says that a retune of the rubric then needs the module regenerated
Adds a test that holds the embedded SOURCE to the .jud file, so a forgotten regeneration fails a test
